sections.h2: Who records deeds in Franklin County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Franklin County Register & Recorder records them, from the Administration Building at 272 North Second Street in Chambersburg, PA 17201. The phone is 717-261-3872 and the fax is 717-709-7211.

One office wears several hats. Besides land records, deeds and mortgages, it handles probate for executors and administrators, records military discharges, and acts as the collection agent for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue on state realty transfer tax and inheritance tax.

Franklin County was carved out of Cumberland County in 1784 and named for Benjamin Franklin. A deed signed at a Franklin County closing finishes its trip here, where it becomes part of the land record searched by every later buyer, lender and title agent.

sections.h2: How can a deed be submitted in Franklin County?
sections.html:
The county accepts deeds by e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, by mail, or in person at the Chambersburg office. Department hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays.

Searching is done remotely through Landex, and questions about that system go to 717-274-5890. Probate filings are by appointment only, which does not apply to recording.

  • E-recording: Simplifile, CSC or EPN, with electronic rejection notices that explain the reason.
  • Mail or overnight delivery: rejected documents come back unrecorded with a written explanation.
  • In person: the clerk reviews the document at the counter before it is accepted.

In each case the county scans the document and sends it to the Tax Assessment Office for UPI certification, then it comes back to the recorder for recording. The UPI stamp prints on the ending page. A document with a missing or wrong parcel number is returned with a note on what to fix.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Franklin County?
sections.html:
A deed or a mortgage is $92.75 on the schedule posted for July 2026, and every document is priced at four pages and four names. The listed fees already include one UPI certification, and each extra certification adds $20.00.

Franklin County Recorder of Deeds fees for common home-sale documents

Deed$92.75
Deed of distribution (Statement of Value required)$92.75
Mortgage$92.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$81.75

Source: Franklin County Register & Recorder fee schedule on franklincountypa.gov.

Beyond those, each page past four costs $2.00 and each name past four costs $0.50. Copies are $0.25 per page, copies of subdivisions $0.50, and certification of a document $1.50. The posted schedule is also marked with a common level ratio of 13.89 for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

sections.h2: How does realty transfer tax work on a Franklin County deed?
sections.html:
The county schedule states that a state tax of 1% and a local tax of the same amount are due at recording. Together that is 2% of the price, or of the assessed value where no price applies.

Every deed must either state the true consideration or carry a Statement of Value. If a full or partial exemption is claimed, the Statement of Value is mandatory unless the deed itself notes the exemption, and it must be fully completed. Corrective deeds and any deed recorded more than 30 days after signing also require one.

  • A deed of distribution from an estate requires a Statement of Value.
  • A property in two or more taxing districts must show the value in each district on the deed so the local share lands in the right place.
  • Pennsylvania lists family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units among the exempt categories.

The state's Department of Revenue says both grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable, so an unpaid tax can reach either side of a Franklin County sale.

sections.h2: What if the Franklin County house came through an estate?
sections.html:
The same office that records the deed also opens the estate, so an heir can handle both in Chambersburg. Probating requires an appointment, and the deed that moves title out of the estate is recorded as a deed of distribution with a Statement of Value attached.

The Register of Wills side of the posted schedule steps up with the size of the estate. Letters and probate run $30.00 for an estate up to $1,000 and $80.00 for one between $75,001 and $100,000, then $35.00 for each additional $100,000 or fraction. Surcharges apply at probate: a $5.00 automation fee and a $41.25 JCP fee.

  • Short certificates are $5.00 each, and a lender or bank often asks for one.
  • An inheritance tax return or supplemental return is $20.00.
  • Certification of inheritance tax paid is $5.00.
  • An inventory and appraisement is $10.00.

Because the county collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax through this office, an heir who intends to sell the inherited house can finish the estate paperwork and the recording at the same counter.

sections.h2: Which other recordings can matter when a Franklin County house sells?
sections.html:
A deed is the main document, but the schedule shows several others that turn up around a sale. Releasing a loan is recorded as a satisfaction or release of mortgage at $81.75, and a partial release costs the same.

Leases are $38.50 unless they run 30 years, which needs a Statement of Value and costs $79.75. A right of way is $78.75, an installment sales agreement $79.75, and a memorandum $38.50. Farm owners may also record an Ag Security Map at $35.00, and plans on 8.5 by 14 paper are $35.00.

A seller who had a prior mortgage should confirm that its satisfaction was recorded before closing, since a lien that was paid off but never released can still appear in a title search of the Franklin County land record.

sections.h2: Can a Franklin County owner get alerts when a document is recorded against a parcel?
sections.html:
Yes. The Recorder of Deeds offers a free Landex Record Alert that notifies an owner when a document carrying their parcel number is recorded or corrected. Sign-up is by email address or mobile number.

The service keys on the parcel number, which is 20 characters including dots and dashes and appears on a tax bill. The county describes the alert as a courtesy tool and adds that it does not replace an owner's own diligence, paid monitoring or a lawyer. Anyone who suspects fraud is told to contact local law enforcement quickly.

For a seller, the alert is a useful check before listing. An owner who signs up can see any mortgage, easement or release that gets recorded against the parcel while a sale is pending.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about selling a house in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Franklin County is the fastest-growing of the four counties compared by Census QuickFacts, with an estimated 160,652 residents in July 2025, up 3.0% from the April 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is worth $249,800 for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy 73.5% of housing.

Median household income is $77,003, poverty is 9.3%, and the county issued 1,033 building permits in 2025. Fayette County issued 196 that year, Huntingdon 64 and Indiana 40, so Franklin County leads the group in new building by a wide margin.

The county covers 772 square miles of land in the Chesapeake Bay watershed, mostly drained by the Potomac, with Chambersburg at its center. About 55.5% of residents lived in urban areas in 2020. Whoever sells a Franklin County house finishes at the Chambersburg office, so the deed paperwork above is the last item to confirm with the closing agent.

faqs.q: How much is the UPI certification in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The first certification is built into the listed recording fee, and each additional UPI certification is $20.00. A deed covering two parcels therefore adds $20.00 to the posted price.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Franklin County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register & Recorder accepts e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, as well as mail and in-person submissions at the Chambersburg office.

faqs.q: What is the Statement of Value fee in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The Statement of Value is $1.00. It is required when a deed claims an exemption from transfer tax, when a deed is corrective or recorded after 30 days, and for deeds of distribution.

faqs.q: When is the Franklin County recorder open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays. Probate filings need an appointment.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the Landex search system in Franklin County?
faqs.a: Call 717-274-5890 for Landex questions. The Register & Recorder's main line at 717-261-3872 handles recording, fees and probate appointments.
